*.why: Core assigns ids and times. A create call (dashboardCreate, workflowCreate, chatCreate, userThemeCreate, aiProviderCreate) and a dashboardUpdate with captureVersion name in `binds` the id the TS made; the replay binds that token to the id Core answers (the dashboard's, the version's, …), which must have the same prefix (dashboard-, dver-, workflow-, theme-, or none for chats and AI providers) and a v4 uuid. Every other <id:n> token is the GUI's (tab, pane, node and message ids): the replay gives each a v4 uuid of its own, the same one everywhere in the case. Times recorded as <now> are any time the Executor gave during the case, and a <now> in params is sent as a fixed time; seeded times (2024-…) must come back unchanged.

view-state/extensions-tab.why: Extensions tabs stay in the window's row (today the save drops them). The mirror rows are today's, so only the restarted window's load differs: windowStateLoad answers the saved state with the extensions tab (its `expect`), and the window shows it.

view-state/repeated-tab-id.why: The legacy mirror skips a tab whose id repeats within the state instead of failing the save (the window's own row keeps the state as sent). Today the whole save fails on the tabs key and nothing is stored.

view-state/second-window.why: View state is per window (Q12 B): the restarted main window gets its own row back (its windowStateLoad `expect`), where today it loads the last save, the second window's.

view-state/new-window-fallback.why: A new window's active project is the most recently used window's (the main window, on p2: its tab save is the latest write), where today it is lastActiveProjectId (p1, from the second window's switch). windowGet answers p2 (its `expect`); a GUI on Core then loads p2, the project windowGet returned; the replayed step-5 windowStateLoad (p1) is today's lastActiveProjectId path as recorded, so what the window shows isn't the recording. The recording's step 5 calls follow today's p1 path; the corrected entry (5d-2 Task 6b review) holds what a GUI on Core sends: windowActivate(win-3, p2), then p2's loads, whose windowStateLoad copies the main window's p2 row; lastActiveProjectId becomes p2.

workflows/does-not-decode.why: Saved workflows leave the project state: no call deletes a workflow the page didn't load, so the one that doesn't decode stays (today the project save after the load deletes it). Listed too (5d-2 Task 7 probe fix): `workflowsList` answers no bodies, so the page can't tell that one won't decode until it's opened. `workflow-bad` (valid JSON, a bigint cell that won't decode) is in the sidebar, first in rowid order; opening it says it can't be read. A row that isn't JSON (`workflow-garbage`) stays out, as Core skips it.

dashboards/prune-at-0.why: dashboard_version_limit 0 keeps every version, as query_version_limit does (Decision 20, 'Version limits and 0'); versions are numbered MAX(version) + 1 inside the transaction. Today 0 deletes every version and the next one is numbered 1 again.

dashboards/delete-during-pending-edit.why: An update of a missing dashboard is DASHBOARD_NOT_FOUND (call 1, the pan), so the removed dashboard stays removed. Today the pan's whole-row upsert re-inserts it.

dashboards/create-name-taken.why: Dashboard names clash within a project (Q3): trimmed, NFC-normalised and case-folded, " sales " is "Sales" (dash-1).

dashboards/rename-to-taken-name.why: A rename to another dashboard's name is NAME_TAKEN (dash-1), and nothing is written: no version, no rename.

dashboards/create-empty-name.why: Names are trimmed and non-empty: INVALID_ARGUMENT, nothing stored.

dashboards/two-tabs-version-numbers.why: Core numbers a version MAX(version) + 1 inside the update's transaction, and snapshots the stored row: the second window's version is 2, a snapshot of the first window's rename. Today its insert collides with version 1 and fails.

dashboards/create-name-taken-nfd.why: Names compare NFC-normalised: "Cafe" + U+0301 is "Café" (dash-2): NAME_TAKEN, nothing written.

chats/two-tabs-same-chat.why: chatMessagesPut upserts the messages it lists and deletes none: the first window's turn stays. Today the second window's replace deletes it.

settings/editor-keybinding-mode.why: editorKeybindingMode is default, vim or emacs; "hyper" is INVALID_ARGUMENT. settingSet with null deletes the row (today it stores NULL; both read as unset). A refused set shows the stored value again (5d-2 Task 6b review): after step 2 the store shows "vim" where the recording kept "hyper", and still "vim" after step 3 (a write the store does not hear).

settings/pending-changes-enabled.why: pending_changes_enabled is "true" or "false". settingSet with null deletes the row (today it stores NULL; both read as unset).

settings/skipped-update-version.why: No string may hold a NUL (Decision 1). settingSet with null deletes the row (today it stores NULL; both read as unset).

settings/query-version-limit.why: A version limit is a whole number from 0 to 100,000 as text: "0" and "100000" are accepted (keep all; the UI clamps to 10 since 5d-1), "abc" and "100001" are INVALID_ARGUMENT. settingSet with null deletes the row (today it stores NULL; both read as unset).

settings/dashboard-version-limit.why: A version limit is a whole number from 0 to 100,000: "-1" and "1.5" are INVALID_ARGUMENT. settingSet with null deletes the row (today it stores NULL; both read as unset).

settings/license-nudge.why: license_nudge is a JSON object: "[1]" and "nope" are INVALID_ARGUMENT. settingSet with null deletes the row (today it stores NULL; both read as unset).

settings/last-active-project-id.why: lastActiveProjectId is read-only in the settings group: windowActivate writes it (Decision 22).

settings/connection-string-secrets-notic.why: connectionStringSecretsNotice is Core's (Decision 12a): the GUI may only clear it with null, which deletes the row; any other value is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

settings/refused-keys.why: App-state keys are a closed set of typed settings: an unknown key, activeRepoId (the shared repos' own), Core's connectionStringSecrets{Vacuum,Upgraded,Checkpoint} keys and aiSettings (written only through the AI settings calls) are refused by settingSet, and an unknown key or one of Core's by settingGet, with INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the key.

ai-settings/two-tabs-different-providers.why: AI settings are split into targeted calls rewritten from the stored record inside the transaction, so both windows' providers stay. Today the second window's whole-record save drops the first's.

themes/add.why: A user theme call (userThemeCreate, userThemeUpdate, userThemeRemove of a theme not in use) writes only its user_themes row. Today every theme save also writes theme_preferences, which leaves a row holding the defaults on a file that had none; no row reads as the defaults.

themes/update.why: A user theme call (userThemeCreate, userThemeUpdate, userThemeRemove of a theme not in use) writes only its user_themes row. Today every theme save also writes theme_preferences, which leaves a row holding the defaults on a file that had none; no row reads as the defaults.

themes/delete-not-in-use.why: A user theme call (userThemeCreate, userThemeUpdate, userThemeRemove of a theme not in use) writes only its user_themes row. Today every theme save also writes theme_preferences, which leaves a row holding the defaults on a file that had none; no row reads as the defaults.

old-data/ai-settings-array.why: A record that isn't a JSON object reads as the defaults, and the next write stores the defaults plus the change. Today an array's elements are spread into the settings and written back under numeric keys.

old-data/user-theme-does-not-parse.why: Themes are saved one row at a time (userThemeCreate), so the row that doesn't parse stays. Today saveUserThemes replaces every row and drops it. As in every theme case, a theme call doesn't write theme_preferences either (see themePrefsChanges).

old-data/saved-canvases-bad-rows.why: Saved workflows leave the project state: nothing deletes a workflow the page couldn't read. Today the first project save after the load deletes both. Listed too (5d-2 Task 7 probe fix): `workflowsList` answers no bodies, so the page can't tell that one won't decode until it's opened. `workflow-bad` (valid JSON, a bigint cell that won't decode) is in the sidebar, first in rowid order; opening it says it can't be read. A row that isn't JSON (`workflow-garbage`) stays out, as Core skips it.

old-data/onboarding-missing-fields.why: A stored onboarding record reads over the store's six defaults (as a missing record does), and onboardingPatch merges into that, so the write keeps every field. Today the missing fields read as undefined and the next write drops them.

old-data/project-state-canvas-view.why: The legacy mirror writes an activeView of canvas (from before the workflow rename) as workflow, which the frozen baseline turns it into on every open anyway (5d-2 Task 4 review). The window's own row keeps the state as sent, canvas included; today's save wrote canvas back.
